thor prod can silently serve a web build older than merged main: v0.11.1 web changes (favicon, full-width layout) were merged but thor served a pre-0.11.1 bundle until a manual deploy.sh thor on 2026-08-12 — deploys only happen when someone runs deploy/prod/deploy.sh. Before diagnosing web code from live symptoms, verify the served bundle first: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{content_type}" http://192.168.1.146:18080/favicon.svg (text/html = stale SPA fallback, image/svg+xml = current). Chrome also caches favicons per-origin aggressively — hard-refresh before trusting the tab icon as evidence.

2026-08-12 codex-thor, task kind: code audit, TWO runs (01KZVTWZPJVVTAS2KMHR4PXBNF, 01KZVV2WRHA1ZD2H2S5M8JQE1K). Verdict: exemplary honesty, zero audit capability. 2026-08-13 codex-orin run 01KZW2XDR7YD2GER787QZ0K67M (attribution-proof attempt): FAILED - not the actor fault. pr-upkeep loop (2026-08-13, run 01KZXATS1HM63SAQZVHX0K4ZD0): the sweep node declares output path /workspace (absolute) in examples/pr-upkeep/workflow.yaml, but headspace-cli export rejects absolute paths (wants workspace-relative like out.json), so 0/1 artifacts export and the workspace is destroyed with --force — the sweep report JSON never persists anywhere (artifacts table empty, ledger evidence carries measurements only). The fix node must re-run examples/pr-upkeep/sweep.py locally (deterministic, read-only, stdlib-only) to regenerate the bound sweepReport. Fixing the artifact declaration is a separate upkeep item, not done in the S3516 pass (PR #51).

pr-upkeep fix node: ALWAYS check for an existing open PR for the top sweep item before opening a new one (gh pr list --search or check branches like upkeep/*). The sweep reads live SonarCloud/Qodo state, which only clears after a fix PR is MERGED and rescanned — so consecutive loop cycles re-surface the same top item even when a green fix PR already exists. Found live 2026-08-13: cycle for run 01KZXATS opened PR #51 (S3516 blocker, all green); the next cycle (run 01KZXBD3) swept the same item and opened duplicate PR #52, closed in favor of #51. The fix_instruction says open OR UPDATE — update means find and reuse the prior cycle PR. Also noted: the sweep attempt result in the run API carried no artifacts refs (headspace 0.11.0), so the fix node regenerated the report by running examples/pr-upkeep/sweep.py locally — a faithful stand-in since the sweep is read-only against the same live surfaces.

pr-upkeep fix-node idempotency: the sweep re-reports an already-fixed item until its PR merges on main (SonarCloud only clears the issue post-merge, and the flow holds no merge credential). When the fix node receives a top item, FIRST check open PRs (gh pr list) for an existing branch covering it — e.g. cycle run 01KZXC2WRAWPEZ8JARW9TGY3ZS found PR #51 (upkeep/s3516-node-runs-invariant-return) already green and current. The right move is verify (diff, checks, behind-count) + a signed status comment for the human gate, never a duplicate PR or churn commits.

prod.env KEY ORDER is load-bearing and mis-ordering fails SILENTLY (probed 2026-08-16 with docker compose config). docker compose --env-file DOES interpolate env-file values recursively, so NODES_DATABASE_URL=...sslmode=${DATABASE_SSLMODE} resolves — but ONLY if DATABASE_SSLMODE appears EARLIER in the file. Reverse the two lines and compose resolves sslmode= to the empty string and reports NO error; libpq then falls back to its own default, so the stack connects and nobody learns the TLS mode was never applied. install-secrets.sh's fresh-install template happens to emit them in the safe order; any add-if-absent lane appends in whatever order the host's gaps dictate and can produce the unsafe one. Remedy: resolve sslmode on the host and write a LITERAL value, so no placeholder and no ordering dependency exists. thor's live URL already has the literal shape.

deploy/prod/install-secrets.sh's shared PROD_ENV_MERGE silently DROPS any value containing a pipe. The idiom is sed -i "s|^${k}=.*|${line}|"; a replacement line containing | makes sed exit 1 with 'unknown option to s' and leave the file BYTE-IDENTICAL. The remote while-loop runs without set -e, so the key is skipped and the merge still reports success. Every existing key survives only because openssl rand -hex 32 emits no pipe — an OPERATOR-SUPPLIED external-database password is the case that breaks it, and NODES_DATABASE_URL is the key most likely to carry one. tests/deploy/prodenvmerge_test.go pins the loop's exact text and requires exactly ONE copy, so fixing it means editing the shared definition AND updating that test deliberately (owner decision 2026-08-16: fix it once, in the shared definition).

#124 is a GUARD-ORDERING defect, not a missing template — and it reproduced live on orin 2026-08-16. install-secrets.sh DOES template NODES_DATABASE_URL (lines 183 bundled / 187 external), but install_env's guard exits 3 on an existing prod.env unless FORCE_PROD=1, returning BEFORE PROD_ENV_MERGE runs. So a key added to the template after a host was provisioned can NEVER reach that host except by also rotating six live secrets. thor was hand-fixed mid-deploy during the #127 session; orin then failed the same way — deploy.sh orin exited 1 at 'error while interpolating services.worker.environment.NODES_DATABASE_URL', leaving orin's prod-worker-1 on a 43-hour-old image while thor's control plane ran 68024ac. Verified safe: re-running install-secrets.sh does NOT propagate fresh secrets from other lanes (install_codex_bridge_env returns 3 on 'kept' and only rc==0 propagates).

Every schedule-triggered pr-upkeep run fails ~1s after create with attempt status contract_rejected / actor_rejected_input, and it is issue #125, not a sandbox or bridge-staleness problem. A triggered run's input IS the github_pr event payload (number/findings/head_sha/repository) and carries no checkout path, so the claude-code bridge falls back to Config.only_allowed_repo() — which returns None by its documented fail-closed rule whenever repo_allowlist has more than one entry. spark's developer bridge (~/.config/culture-nodes-bridges/developer.json) lists TWO leftover worktrees (owe-developer on ctb/t32, upkeep-lane on upkeep/lane, both merged branches among 16 survivors). Zero tokens are billed. Redeploying thor/orin cannot affect it: the rejecting bridge is on spark and is a live source-tree uv-run install. Which repo a multi-lane bridge should use is #125's OWNER decision, not cleanup.

A worker refuses a PARTIAL NODES_CODE_RUNNER_{NAME,REVISION,ACTOR_ID} tuple and accepts none-at-all, but BOTH prod compose files hardcoded NODES_CODE_RUNNER_NAME while defaulting the other two to empty — making the legitimate 'this deployment runs no code nodes' state unreachable. thor survived only because someone hand-installed the other two; orin had none and CrashLoopBackOff'd (exit 2) the moment a deploy brought it to a revision carrying the check, after 46 hours running fine on an older image. deploy.sh exited 0 and audit-credentials.sh PASSED on a host that could not boot, because the audit is per-key and this is a relationship BETWEEN keys. Fixed 2026-08-16 in PR #137 (squash 737dddc): compose interpolates all three, and install-secrets.sh writes NAME only where the other two already exist — the conditional compose cannot express. LESSON: a fail-closed validation must be checked against every deployment path it would newly refuse; this was the THIRD instance of that pattern in this repo.

2026-08-16: the dev machine's LAN address moved from 192.168.1.157 to 192.168.1.118 and FIVE spark-hosted actors stayed registered at the old one — the four claude-code bridges (8086-8089) and human-inbox (8090). Every dispatch to a spark actor fails to connect while the bridges themselves are healthy. NOTHING detected it: it surfaced only because install-secrets.sh exited 255 on an unreachable ssh target mid-deploy. Issue #136. This is the exact decay the transport inversion exists to retire (docs/decisions/transport-inversion.md, migration 0036 held in migrations/pending/, #121): an address recorded once at registration is a fact that rots silently. Check GET /v1alpha1/actors endpoints against reality before blaming a bridge for a failed dispatch.

Pattern observed strongly on 2026-08-16 (#128/#137 cycle): task subagents given explicit permission to REPORT rather than fix, and told to verify rather than transcribe, corrected the operator's brief three times — (1) two failed runs I claimed shared one cause had identical error classes but DIFFERENT 400 reasons; (2) a defect I called silent was loud today and only becomes silent after the change being made; (3) a 'six secrets' count that is five per host and four in the rotation confirmation text. Each correction came from reading a live source. Also: a test agent scoped to tests only reported three script defects it deliberately did NOT assert on, which became issue #135. PRACTICE: write briefs that state the evidence and invite contradiction, scope agents to one file, and tell them explicitly 'report, do not fix, and do not bend a test to match the code'.

2026-08-16: `git reset --hard origin/main` in culture-nodes silently destroyed three uncommitted eidetic records in .eidetic/memory/culture-nodes__public.jsonl. This repo's memory is IN-REPO (CLAUDE.md: a plain /remember lands in <repo-root>/.eidetic/memory, committed and mesh-shared), so /remember writes are working-tree changes that any destructive git command will eat. git status listed them and I ran the reset anyway. PRACTICE: commit or stash .eidetic/memory before any reset --hard / checkout -f / clean, and re-verify records survived afterwards with a grep for their ids.

Migration 0036 (drop actors.endpoint_ref + runner_invocations.endpoint) CANNOT ship in the same release as the code that stops using the columns, and its ADR 0002 bypass is now WITHDRAWN in the file itself (#143). The premise was measured and is false: deploy.sh takes ONE host argument, the migrate service exists only in compose.thor.yml, and orin's N-1 worker reads actors.endpoint_ref via DBRegistry.Resolve AND reads/writes runner_invocations.endpoint via internal/store/postgres/runnerasync.go. So `deploy.sh thor` migrates and leaves orin on the previous binary against the migrated schema. Required sequence: keep columns, ship code that stops using them, deploy to BOTH hosts, THEN apply the drop in a LATER release, then deploy that to orin. migrations_test.go was inverted to pin the withdrawal and FORBID the old premise reappearing as prose. Established by codex-thor run 01M05ZG7GNPZM96RKNR6RBW4B1.

Dial-in cannot be enabled on more than one bridge per host as shipped (#147). dialin.configured() reads PREFIX_CONTROL_PLANE_URL/_ACTOR_KEY/_DIAL_TOKEN from os.environ ONLY, the prefix is per-BACKEND not per-bridge, and spark's four claude bridges share one systemd EnvironmentFile (~/.culture-nodes/bridge-push.env). thor/orin each run one codex bridge, which is why the gap stayed hidden. A per-bridge systemd drop-in works but LEAKS the credential: `systemctl --user show <unit> -p Environment` prints it in full, and so does /proc/<pid>/environ - and a dispatched claude -p session runs with the bridge's own privileges (confinement: none), so a session could read sibling bridges' credentials. Per-bridge JSON config is the right destination, but it does NOT exist uniformly: claude-code and human-inbox have per-bridge JSON, codex has one JSON per host, notify is EnvironmentFile-only.

2026-08-16: the FIRST production dial-in this deployment has ever had. inbound_authentication had ZERO rows before it - dial-in shipped in code (t23 mixed mode) and had never been used. company/developer was given an operator-generated credential (digest only stored) and a per-bridge systemd drop-in pointing at the control plane over the TAILNET, and run 01M063JW8M1G0NSVZY6MFT3DJV completed: one inbound_actor_mailbox row, claimed->completed in 36ms, real claude session, ledger record. Motivated by #136 recurring live mid-cycle - both spark NICs stayed UP with the same addresses but thor could reach neither, and tailscale fell back from a direct LAN route to relay. Caveat recorded honestly: the LAN recovered before the post-check, so concurrency with the outage is not precisely bounded; the mailbox row is what carries the argument.

Running the new merge-gate's PINNED matrix against real work (100 changed files, 10 gates) found three defects its own tests did not - strong evidence that a gate must be exercised, not just unit-tested. (1) #152: the pinned adapter-lint command is `uv run flake8 adapters`, which walks into the .venv dirs uv run creates - 40912 findings on a machine that has run the adapter tests, 12 on a clean checkout. A digest-pinned matrix whose verdict depends on the filesystem defeats the point of pinning. (2) #153: scripts/merge-gate.py's local_outcome decides in one loop with early returns, so the FIRST decisive gate in matrix order wins; [failing,missing-tool]->changes_required but [missing-tool,failing]->measurement_incomplete. internal/handover.GateResults.Outcome is correct (counts.Failed checked first). Fail-safe (the disagreement refuses) but makes changes_required effectively unreachable. (3) #148: unknown matrix keys accepted silently, so a typo in `reaches` becomes a silent not_applicable. NOTE the schema: reaches takes GLOBS (**/*.go), requires not tools, measurement not threshold.

deploy/prod/register-actor.sh used to rebuild each new revision's metadata from a hardcoded {"auth_token_env": ...} literal. Actor rows are APPEND-ONLY, so every registration writes a new row - meaning any other metadata key was one registration away from being erased, including handover_remote which the address cutover depends on. It also hardcoded kind='agent'/protocol='http' (so it could not register company/human-ops at all) and its idempotency check compared only endpoint+auth_token_env, so a metadata-only change reported 'unchanged' and wrote nothing. Fixed (#142) with INSERT ... SELECT ... metadata || overlay so the merge happens inside Postgres and stored JSON never round-trips through the shell. New flag: --metadata KEY=VALUE (repeatable). Verified in production: company/developer revision 2 carries BOTH auth_token_env and repository_identity. To run it from spark: PSQL_CMD="docker exec -i prod-postgres-1 psql -U nodes -d nodes" on thor.

2026-08-16, three analysis dispatches, all graded 5 - codex on read-only analysis is now a proven, high-value lane. codex-thor 01M05ZG7GNPZM96RKNR6RBW4B1 (ADR bypass re-justification): VERIFIED the operator's premise instead of accepting it, found the scheduler was omitted from the migration's own text, and established the decisive fact nobody had checked (orin's N-1 worker reads both dropped columns), with file:line for every claim and a ready-to-paste replacement. codex-orin 01M05ZGNT86MAFDHATB6W5VYPN (toolchain measurement): CAUGHT AN OPERATOR ERROR - my ssh-login probe reported orin lacking uv and go, but a dispatched session's real PATH has both in ~/.local/bin; also found preflight.py is tool-agnostic (names = list(argv)) so adding node/npm to TOOLS was the entire change. codex-thor 01M05ZH6AW6TFDSESF3B0GKD3A (concurrency disposition): chose INSTRUMENT from the code, traced the window with commit-qualified refs, answered the billing question directly. PATTERN: give codex a question with a decision to make and files to cite, and it outperforms; all three stated their own limitations unprompted (their checkout was on ctb/t17b and lacked files, so they read from named commits).
